findings.body:
<!-- proofline:finding-series=01a202cc-2f54-76e7-9ab9-073e404d3f78 -->
**Serious** · Concurrent startup can abort a console command during migration 002

Two invocations can read schema version 1 before either migrates. The second then runs `002_retire_format.sql` after the first commits, trying to drop `legacy_format` again.

SQLite raises an error before the second invocation dispatches its command.

Acquire a write transaction with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before reading `user_version`, and apply migrations without releasing that transaction.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The duplicate column drop on a version-1 database is new: before this change there was no migration 002. The older runner could race on initial table creation, but that is a different failing statement.

</details>

[View finding in Proofline](https://proofline.sh/orgs/by-id/01a202a0-cd61-7684-99bc-53c775b0de50/reviews/01a202ca-78bf-77f0-81e8-2480bb047772/findings/01a202cc-2f58-7525-b219-864a9a37ef3e)

findings.author: prooflinedev[bot]
findings.body:
<!-- proofline:finding-series=01a202cc-2f56-7619-bab4-e0434daa424f -->
**Warning** · First history page waits for a full deliveries table rewrite

On a version-1 database, `history --limit 1` runs the new `DROP COLUMN` migration before fetching the page.

The command now waits for work proportional to the stored size of `deliveries`, rather than reading at most two rows after a version check.

Run schema upgrades in an explicit upgrade step instead of during `history`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Before this change, an initialized version-1 database skipped the only migration. This change adds a transaction that rewrites the stored rows to remove the column and commits before the history query runs. The page limit does not bound that one-time work.

</details>

[View finding in Proofline](https://proofline.sh/orgs/by-id/01a202a0-cd61-7684-99bc-53c775b0de50/reviews/01a202ca-78bf-77f0-81e8-2480bb047772/findings/01a202cc-2f60-77df-bea4-cc73ff4258f5)
